signals.name: weighted_directional_level_shift
signals.measurement_meaning: Signed aligned level shift under W, attenuated by one plus B input variance. Allows implementation-specific directional sensitivity to vary with input variance.
signals.limitation: The variance attenuation is a proposed functional form. Two tasks cannot establish its transferability or a causal effect.
signals.falsifying_response: On additional held-out tasks, W-minus-S Y differences show no consistent dependence on this measurement, and adding it fails to reduce task-balanced prediction error.

signals.name: optimizer_exposure_level_mismatch
signals.measurement_meaning: Optimizer exposure interaction multiplied by combined training-group level distance from B, attenuated by one plus B input variance.
signals.limitation: Combined level distance discards group direction and does not measure gradient mismatch. Its association with implementation penalties may be specific to the supplied tasks.
signals.falsifying_response: Across new tasks, larger values fail to accompany more negative W-minus-S Y responses, or the augmented ridge fails to improve held-out prediction error.

reasoning: The supplied feedback shows a larger W-associated Y penalty in one task, especially for positive aligned level shift; its Z also decreases under W in both directions. These motivate separate directional and exposure–mismatch measurements. Both introduce nonpolynomial interactions beyond the existing quadratic terms without using task identity. They are unvalidated candidates: no fitted improvement, hidden-task result, or causal confirmation is claimed.
